candidate.answerReason: The roots have product 8, and their nonzero difference gives \((r_1+r_2)^2=(r_1-r_2)^2+32>32\).

methods.label: Use the nonzero difference of the roots
methods.explanation:
The condition that the real roots are distinct gives a strictly positive square: \((r_1-r_2)^2>0\). We can connect this to their sum using their product.

Factoring the monic quadratic by its two roots gives
\[
(x-r_1)(x-r_2)
=x^2-(r_1+r_2)x+r_1r_2.
\]
Its constant term must agree with that of \(x^2+px+8\), so \(r_1r_2=8\). Expanding the squares now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(r_1+r_2)^2
&=(r_1-r_2)^2+4r_1r_2\\
&=(r_1-r_2)^2+32>32.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking nonnegative square roots yields
\[
\lvert r_1+r_2\rvert>\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt2.
\]
The inequality is strict precisely because the roots are distinct. Thus choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\) must hold.
methods.levelReason: The proof uses root-coefficient relations, elementary square identities, and the positivity of a nonzero real square.

methods.label: Use the positive discriminant
methods.explanation:
The discriminant tells us when a quadratic has two distinct real roots. For this equation it is
\[
\Delta=p^2-4\cdot1\cdot8=p^2-32.
\]
The stated root condition requires \(\Delta>0\), so \(p^2>32\) and hence \(\lvert p\rvert>4\sqrt2\).

To connect \(p\) to the requested sum, expand the factors determined by the roots:
\[
(x-r_1)(x-r_2)
=x^2-(r_1+r_2)x+r_1r_2.
\]
Comparing the coefficient of \(x\) with the given quadratic gives \(r_1+r_2=-p\). Therefore
\[
\lvert r_1+r_2\rvert=\lvert p\rvert>4\sqrt2,
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The discriminant and root-sum relation are standard school quadratic facts, with no explicit root calculation required.

candidate.annotationRationale: Both methods connect an expression in the roots to the quadratic's coefficients. The first obtains strictness from the squared root difference; the second obtains it from the discriminant. Those are alternative method-local ideas. Factor expansion and the relation between square roots and absolute values support both.

review.mathematicalCheck: Factor expansion gives r₁r₂=8, so (r₁+r₂)²=(r₁-r₂)²+32>32. Independently, distinct real roots require p²-32>0, and r₁+r₂=-p gives the same strict bound. Both establish |r₁+r₂|>4√2.
review.levelCheck: Both methods explain the coefficient relations and strict inequality using standard school quadratic facts.
review.methodDistinctness: The nonzero root-difference argument and the discriminant argument provide useful alternative viewpoints at the same level.
